newsitem.title: USA: TCI Satellite readies 1st junk bond deal.
newsitem.headline: TCI Satellite readies 1st junk bond deal.

text.p: TCI Satellite Entertainment (TSAT), plans to debut in the junk bond market with a $350 million offering of high-yield bonds over the next several weeks, a TCI spokeswoman said.
Proceeds will be used to finance continued growth of the company's various interests in medium- and high-powered digital broadcast satellite (DBS) services, she said.

A high-yield cable and media analyst said, "I think DBS is viewed as a real serious threat to cable right now. People on the Street really view this as a viable business, especially in rural areas and areas away from large cities where cable has not penetrated. This should be a very popular deal." TSAT holds a 20.9 percent interest in Primestar, the second largest DBS provider in the U.S. and a user of medium-powered DBS technology.
TSAT plans to launch its first high-power DBS satellite in early March.
The company was spun off from Tele-Communications Inc in December of 1996. Soon after, the company arranged $750 million in senior secured bank financing.

The high-yield market is not unfamiliar with DBS companies, analysts note. Pegasus Communications Corp, the largest franchisee of DirectTV DBS service, sold $150 exchangeable preferred stock earlier this month. EchoStar Communications Corp DISH.O sold $330 million in zero-coupon junk bonds in May of 1994 and $350 million of zeros in March of 1996.

The upcoming TSAT deal will consist of $200 million in senior subordinated discount notes due 2006 and $150 million in senior subordinated notes due 2006, market sources say. The TSAT spokeswoman declined to comment on the structure.
Merrill Lynch & Co and Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp, have been chosen as joint-lead managers for the 144a private placement transaction.
